newsitem.title: GERMANY: KLM ups Germany to India rates 60-90pct.
newsitem.headline: KLM ups Germany to India rates 60-90pct.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV said it will raise air cargo rates from Germany to India by up to 90 percent from January 15.
Oliver Evans, sales director Central & Eastern Europe, said the airline would follow rises announced by Lufthansa Cargo AG and Air India (AIN.CN).
"From January 15, our prices will be increased by 60-90 percent out of Germany to India," he told Reuters in an interview.
"Our prices had fallen to uneconomic levels because of the negative developments on the markets," he added.
But high demand and reduced capacity now gave an opportunity to raise rates from their present low levels.
KLM had completely cut its freighter services to India in recent months after introducing them last year on the back of a booming market, Evans said.
"It is a very volatile market and that is why we have withdrawn the freighters," he added.
KLM dropped its Delhi freighter in July, Bombay and one of two Madras freighters were stopped in October and the second Madras freighter ended in November.
Evans said other airlines had also withdrawn India capacity in recent months.
But he stressed: "Export markets into India have remained very strong and there is a lot of cargo still moving into India from Germany.
"KLM is a very strong player. It is one of the markets where we have one of the highest market shares," he added.
Lufthansa Cargo announced on December 5 it would raise Germany to India rates by between 15 and 70 percent according to destination and weight category from January 1.
Air India said the same day it planned to match the rates rise. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
